summary: json-schema-inspector fetches and executes an obfuscated remote payload from a hardcoded C2 on every call to its exported validator API
details: The package advertises itself as a JSON/XML schema validator, but lib/core.js exports a trigger() routine invoked by validateJson() and validateXml() on every call. trigger() first runs a sandbox-evasion check (aborts when host uptime is under 300 seconds, fewer than 2 CPUs, or under 2GB RAM), then reconstructs a hardcoded command-and-control URL that is stored XOR-encoded with key 0x55 and resolves to https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/cryptonomad411/cool-utils/package.json. It fetches a JSON manifest from that host, selects a per-platform entry (Windows/Linux/macOS), AES-256-CBC-decrypts a bundled bootstrap script using a runtime-derived static key, and spawns the decrypted script as a detached background process with stdio ignored: spawn(process.execPath, ['-e', childScript]) on Windows and spawn('sh', ['-c', script]) on Linux/macOS at lib/core.js lines 90 and 107. The combination of XOR-hidden C2, AES-encrypted per-OS loader payloads, sandbox-evasion gating, and detached child-process execution provides remote code execution on any host that installs the package and invokes its documented validator API, under attacker-controlled content that can change at any time on the jsdelivr-mirrored GitHub repository.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
